Project.Name: attribute-driven-migration.xml
Project.Title: Attribute-Driven Migration: The Cross-Track Attribute Foundation

Task.Name: Phase 0 — Read the tree
A0.1 OU tree exported read-only: placement and size, GPO links at domain, OU and site, inheritance, and hand-made delegations; every OU and each GPO half tagged with its track
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#stage-0-read-what-the-ou-tree-encodes

Task.Name: A0.2 A decision for every security group: keep synced, convert to cloud-only, convert to dynamic, or retire
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with application owners Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#the-per-group-decision

Task.Name: A0.3 OU-to-unit mapping drafted: which OU delegations become administrative units, and which become Azure RBAC scopes for servers
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#organizational-units

Task.Name: A0.4 GPO settings split by track: user halves to the HR track's policy design, computer halves to the Endpoint plan
Task.Contact: Identity engineering, with the endpoint lead
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with the endpoint lead Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#four-tracks

Task.Name: X-EG0 Device and server observation signed off (Endpoint plan, Gate 0)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO (Endpoint plan) If decided late: The Endpoint plan triages Group Policy without knowing which halves belong to people Source: endpoint-device.md

Task.Name: X-NG0 Non-person identities inventoried (Non-Person Identity plan, Gate 0)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO (Non-Person Identity plan) If decided late: Service accounts in the tree are inventoried without their OU placement and delegations Source: non-person-identity.md

Task.Name: AG0 Gate 0 — The tree read
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering lead Criteria: Inventory in Git, site-linked GPOs included; every OU and every GPO half tagged with its track; a decision for every group; the OU-to-unit mapping drafted; nothing changed in the forest Source: ../books/b02-identity/10-migrating-and-governing.md#phase-0-assessment

Task.Name: X-G0 Program G0 — Ready to Plan: the read-only assessment committed
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Steward (program) If decided late: The program plans Phase 1 without knowing what the OU tree encodes Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: Phase 1 — Schema and slots
A1.1 AD attribute inventory: which attributes are populated, by whom and how fully; which extension attributes are free to carry codes
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#compared-with-active-directory

Task.Name: X-DI1 Enterprise person key, and how source keys map to it (Identity Lifecycle plan, D-I1)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ICAM governance body (Identity Lifecycle plan) If decided late: The mapping has no key to carry in employeeId Source: identity-lifecycle.md

Task.Name: A1.2 AD-to-Entra mapping for every attribute that drives access, per object type: users, devices, Arc servers, service principals; the store for each from the store table
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Data architect, with identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#the-attribute-stores-in-the-order-to-reach-for-them

Task.Name: X-I12 Attribute authority map signed (Identity Lifecycle plan, I1.2)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ICAM governance body (Identity Lifecycle plan) If decided late: The schema can't name a writer for an attribute whose authority isn't decided Source: identity-lifecycle.md

Task.Name: D-A1 Attribute schema: the store and the single writer for every attribute that drives access, in all four tracks
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Data architect Options: Native properties first, then extension attributes 1–15 for what rules read, directory extensions for more slots, custom security attributes for sensitive values rules don't need, device properties, Azure tags and certificateUserIds (the store table); or a broader use of directory extensions from the start If decided late: No slot can be assigned, and every group rule, persona and targeting convention waits Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#attributes

Task.Name: D-A2 The coded slot register: which extension attribute carries which code, on users and on devices
Task.Contact: Data architect, with HR for the code lists
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Data architect, with HR for the code lists Options: The program attribute map (organization, worker type and position category in extensionAttribute10 to 12; region, cost center, division, account type, clearance and DoNotSync in their slots; device tier, role and environment on the device object); or an agency map that keeps the same rule: codes, never names, one writer per slot If decided late: Rules and filters are written against slots that may move, and every one is rewritten later Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/06-canonical-attribute-schema.md#program-attribute-map

Task.Name: A1.3 Slot register published: one writer per slot, the code list owner, what reads it; the help desk, self-service and Exchange write paths listed for removal
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Data architect Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/06-canonical-attribute-schema.md#writers

Task.Name: A1.4 Device, server and non-person attribute authorities named: the procurement record through the Autopilot group tag, the asset record through Arc onboarding tags, the owning system's record
Task.Contact: Data architect, with the endpoint lead
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Data architect, with the endpoint lead Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#stage-1-source-the-attributes

Task.Name: AG1 Gate 1 — Schema and slots signed
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ICAM governance body Criteria: Every attribute that drives access has one store, one writer and one owner, in all four tracks; the slot register published; the person key carried in employeeId in both directories; codes, never display names, in anything a rule reads Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/12-execution-plan.md#phase-1-attribute-authority-and-schema

Task.Name: X-P11 Attribute taxonomy finalized (program P1.1)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Data architect (program) If decided late: The program's taxonomy is finalized without the cross-track slot register Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: Phase 2 — Prove the attributes
X-I15 HR data baselined; employeeId populated; orphan candidates owned (Identity Lifecycle plan, I1.5)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: HR data steward (Identity Lifecycle plan) If decided late: The coverage baseline measures data the HR plan hasn't yet corrected Source: identity-lifecycle.md

Task.Name: A2.1 Coverage baseline across the tracks: uncorrelated accounts, empty coded slots, counts per organization code against an HR export, duplicate keys; device and server attribute coverage
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#stage-2-prove-the-attributes-are-true-before-anything-depends-on-them

Task.Name: D-A3 Correlation threshold before any rule grants access
Task.Contact: Authorizing official, through the agency's risk governance
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Authorizing official, through the agency's risk governance Options: 99% of the pilot cohort correlated (a proposed starting point); a risk-tiered threshold, stricter for privileged and leaver-sensitive populations; 100% with a dated exception list If decided late: No group can be piloted, because nobody has said how true the attributes must be Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/12-execution-plan.md#sequencing-principle

Task.Name: A2.2 Other write paths removed: help desk and self-service edits to the access slots, Exchange custom-attribute cmdlets, write rights on the target OUs
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with security Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/06-canonical-attribute-schema.md#writers

Task.Name: A2.3 Entra ID sign-in, audit and provisioning logs routed outside Entra ID before the pilot's first change
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Security operations Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/11-drift-metrics-and-evidence.md#the-evidence-each-event-leaves

Task.Name: AG2 Gate 2 — Attributes proven for the pilot
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: Correlation threshold met on the pilot cohort; every enabled account correlated or on a dated exception list; no duplicate keys; every other write path to the access slots removed in AD and Entra ID; logs leaving Entra ID Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/12-execution-plan.md#phase-1-attribute-authority-and-schema

Task.Name: Phase 3 — Sync
A3.1 Sync mapping for the slot register: carriers in the provisioning apps' target lists, date mappings, the transitional account-type rule, the DoNotSync filter; soft and hard match blocked
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#stage-3-map-the-attributes-through-sync

Task.Name: X-P17 Sync and DNS Private Resolver designs (program P1.7)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering (program) If decided late: The sync design is approved without the attribute flow for the coded slots Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: X-IG3 HR feed live for the foundation scope, shadow differences explained (Identity Lifecycle plan, Gate 3)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO (Identity Lifecycle plan) If decided late: The coded slots have no live writer, so the group library can't be shadowed on real data Source: identity-lifecycle.md

Task.Name: AG3 Gate 3 — Attributes flowing
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering lead Criteria: Object counts within ±1%; no sync errors; every slot in the register arrives in Entra ID with the value HR sent; shadow-mode differences explained; both match types blocked outside a planned window Source: ../books/b02-identity/10-migrating-and-governing.md#phase-1-sync-deployment-and-initial-sync

Task.Name: Phase 4 — Groups and administrative units
A4.1 Dynamic user group library: node and functional rules on codes; every access rule guarded by accountEnabled and userType and excluding agents' accounts; nesting flattened; no memberOf
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with application owners Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#stage-4-materialize-ou-subtrees-as-dynamic-groups

Task.Name: A4.2 Rules checked before they exist in production: guards, codes not names, paused processing; each rule tested against named users
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b06-data-platform/17-dynamic-membership-delegation-and-privilege.md#writing-naming-and-testing-rules

Task.Name: D-A4 Restricted management, unit by unit, before each unit exists
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Options: No (the default): the unit scopes writes and stays in governance automation; yes, for a small set of sensitive accounts, accepting that they leave PIM, entitlement management, Lifecycle Workflows and access reviews If decided late: A unit is created without the decision, and restriction can't be changed afterward Source: ../books/b02-identity/05-delegation-without-ous.md#restricted-management-a-per-au-decision

Task.Name: A4.3 Unit registry: tenant readers, department and division units whose rules mirror the group rules; scoped roles to PIM-eligible role-assignable groups; each unit created before the groups it holds
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#stage-5-delegate-with-administrative-units

Task.Name: AG4 Gate 4 — Group library and units designed
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering lead Criteria: Every governed group on one of the two patterns, on codes, with guards; every unit rule mirroring its group rule; restriction decided for every unit; every role assignment in the matrix Source: ../books/b01-transformation-arc/04-identity-transformation.md#verification

Task.Name: X-P12 Dynamic group design tested; enterprise groups and administrative units built (program P1.2)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering (program) If decided late: The program builds groups and units from a design that hasn't been checked Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: X-P21S Pilot attributes, groups and units going live (program P2.1, its start)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering (program) If decided late: There's no live pilot data to shadow the rules against Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: A4.4 Shadow comparison on the pilot: each dynamic group against the group it replaces, every add and remove explained; membership-delta alerts on
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with application owners Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#dynamic-user-groups-hr-track

Task.Name: X-P22 Pilot Conditional Access and Intune policies assigned (program P2.2, its start)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering (program) If decided late: Policies are assigned to groups whose membership hasn't been reconciled Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: Phase 5 — Personas and targeting conventions
A5.1 Conditional Access personas from coded attributes (worker type for internals and externals); every grant paired with a block; empty-slot users reported; emergency access excluded
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#stage-6-replace-gpo-inheritance-with-conditional-access-and-intune-targeting

Task.Name: D-A5 The persona set the Conditional Access library targets
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Options: The program's personas, built from the worker type and account type codes; personas plus division-specific overlays; fewer personas with more exclusions (not recommended) If decided late: The Conditional Access design runs in report-only without the groups it will enforce on Source: ../books/b04-access/03-the-conditional-access-model.md#naming-and-the-persona-model

Task.Name: X-P15 Conditional Access design running in report-only (program P1.5)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering (program) If decided late: Report-only runs against personas that may change Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: A5.2 Device targeting conventions: device slots written at registration by the provisioning service; dynamic device groups only where a rule reads tier or role; filters otherwise; no dynamic device group as an exclusion
Task.Contact: Endpoint lead, with the data architect
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead, with the data architect Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#intune-track

Task.Name: X-E12 Intune policy library built unassigned, with groups, filters and scope tags (Endpoint plan, E1.2, its start)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Endpoint lead (Endpoint plan) If decided late: The policy library is built on targeting the foundation may change Source: endpoint-device.md

Task.Name: A5.3 Server targeting conventions: the Arc tag taxonomy drawn from the asset record and aligned with the device slots; resource groups as the delegation scope
Task.Contact: Server infrastructure, with the data architect
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Server infrastructure, with the data architect Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#arc-track

Task.Name: X-E42 Tag taxonomy fixed from the asset record (Endpoint plan, E4.2)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Server infrastructure (Endpoint plan) If decided late: Arc servers are tagged with a taxonomy the device and user sides don't share Source: endpoint-device.md

Task.Name: A5.4 Non-person conventions: owners and sponsors recorded by the enterprise person key; custom security attributes for service principals (system, environment, tier) defined
Task.Contact: Identity engineering, with the identity governance officer
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with the identity governance officer Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#what-microsoft-documents-for-targeting-service-principals-by-attribute-partly

Task.Name: X-N12 AI accountability: sponsors mastered in HR (Non-Person Identity plan, N1.2, its start)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity governance officer (Non-Person Identity plan) If decided late: Sponsors are recorded by name rather than by key, and a sponsor's move or departure can't be matched Source: non-person-identity.md

Task.Name: AG5 Gate 5 — Targeting conventions set
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: Personas from authoritative codes, grant and block in pairs, empty slots reported; device and server conventions published and handed to the Endpoint plan; non-person owners and sponsors keyed to the person key Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#attribute-to-mechanism-crosswalk

Task.Name: Phase 6 — PIV and CAC binding
A6.1 Binding coverage measured: certificateUserIds or altSecurityIdentities present and correct for every pilot card holder; the card management system named as the binding writer
Task.Contact: Identity engineering, with the PIV program office
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with the PIV program office Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#pki-binding

Task.Name: D-A6 Required affinity binding for PIV and CAC
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Options: High affinity in production (the program's position), with a custom rule per issuer during the pilot; low affinity until coverage is complete, with a dated end; mixed by issuer If decided late: PIV sign-in goes to the pilot at the tenant default, which is low affinity Source: ../books/b07-pki/06-device-and-user-certificates.md#username-bindings-and-affinity

Task.Name: A6.2 High affinity piloted on the pilot cohort before the tenant setting changes; multifactor binding rule by issuer or policy OID
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/09-credentials-and-certificates.md#binding-the-piv-certificate-to-the-entra-user

Task.Name: X-P28 Certificate-based authentication for PIV and CAC holders (program P2.8)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering (program) If decided late: PIV sign-in reaches the pilot with bindings nobody has measured Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: D-A7 Who writes the binding after AD
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ICAM governance body Options: The card management system writes certificateUserIds through Microsoft Graph at issuance (design guidance, an open pilot); Entra Connect keeps syncing from altSecurityIdentities while any AD remains; manual entry by a Privileged Authentication Administrator (not at scale) If decided late: User issuance can't move off AD CS, because nothing writes the binding without AD Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#pki-binding

Task.Name: X-P45 User and device issuance off AD CS; smart-card logon GPO retired (program P4.5)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: PKI lead (program) If decided late: Issuance moves off AD CS with no writer for the binding Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: AG6 Gate 6 — PIV binding proven on the pilot
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: Every pilot card holder bound; high affinity piloted with no lockouts; phishing-resistant strength for CBA users; the leaver removes the binding as well as revoking the card Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#pki-binding

Task.Name: Phase 7 — The mover proof
X-I43 Joiner and mover automation (Identity Lifecycle plan, I4.3)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering (Identity Lifecycle plan) If decided late: There's no mover workflow to prove the foundation against Source: identity-lifecycle.md

Task.Name: A7.1 Mover proof on the pilot: one personnel action moves a test user's organization code; groups, unit, persona and access packages change with no ticket; the device stays put; a drift scan comes back clean
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with HR Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#worked-example-one-user-and-one-mover-event

Task.Name: AG7 Gate 7 — Mover proven across the tracks
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: The test mover's access changed only through the attributes, within the measured latency; nothing assigned by hand; the device's groups unchanged; the sponsor of any non-person identity the user sponsors notified; the change traced from the personnel action to the drift report Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#worked-example-one-user-and-one-mover-event

Task.Name: X-G2 Program G2 — Pilot Clean
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Steward (program) If decided late: The pilot is called clean without a mover having been proved Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: Phase 8 — Cut-over and the OU tree
A8.1 Wave scopes written as attribute queries whose groups already exist; leaver automation first in every wave
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#stage-7-cut-over-in-phases

Task.Name: X-D07 Wave plan: which divisions, in which order (program D07)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor (program) If decided late: Waves are drawn by OU, not by attribute value Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: A8.2 Per-wave attribute gate: coverage of the wave's query, shadow diff, a dry run with writes off, then seven days in which every change traces to HR before the ticket path closes
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/appendix-c-acceptance-and-cutover.md#proving-hr-is-the-sole-source

Task.Name: X-P31 Wave 1, first region (program P3.1)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering (program) If decided late: Wave 1 closes with no attribute gate Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: X-IG5 Populations cloud-mastered (Identity Lifecycle plan, Gate 5)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: ISSO (Identity Lifecycle plan) If decided late: Shown for reference: the HR plan's own cut-over Source: identity-lifecycle.md

Task.Name: X-G3 Program G3 — Rollout Complete
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Steward (program) If decided late: The transitional sync rules that read OU placement can't come out while any population still depends on them Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: A8.3 Transitional rules removed: the account-type sync rule that reads OU placement, OU-based scoping filters and the provisioning OU computation for cloud-mastered populations
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b02-identity/09-building-the-entra-target.md#attribute-flow-and-transformations

Task.Name: X-P42 OU-based security groups retired (program P4.2)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering (program) If decided late: The OU tree still grants access through its groups Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: A8.4 OU tree frozen: hand-made delegations removed; no OU drives access, scoping or policy; the tree's final export archived in Git as the record
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/b01-transformation-arc/04-identity-transformation.md#phase-4-legacy-retirement

Task.Name: AG8 Gate 8 — OU tree retired as a control
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: Every population cut over by attribute query with its gate passed; no sync rule, scoping filter, group, delegation or policy reads OU placement; the final tree archived; rollback by re-enabling, never by re-creating Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#stage-7-cut-over-in-phases

Task.Name: X-P51 AD changes frozen; final assessment (program P5.1, its start)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Steward (program) If decided late: AD is frozen while something still reads the OU tree Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: Phase 9 — Drift, limits and steady state
D-A8 Drift severity and response times
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Options: The program's classes (missing identity, stale access, orphan, attribute drift, unauthorized write, credential drift, schema drift) with high severity closed in days and the rest on a dated plan; a stricter clock for unauthorized writes to the access slots If decided late: Drift findings pile up with nobody obliged to close them Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/11-drift-metrics-and-evidence.md#drift-between-hr-and-the-directory

Task.Name: A9.1 Drift scans scheduled: HR against the directory, the unit and role registry against the tenant, membership deltas; each track's own reconciliation pointed at the same findings queue
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Security operations Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#stage-8-detect-and-correct-drift

Task.Name: X-P211 Drift-clean hold on the pilot (program P2.11, its start)
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Steward (program) If decided late: The drift-clean hold has no scan to measure it Source: program-master-schedule.md

Task.Name: A9.2 Limits register: dynamic group and rule limits, the 100-workflow Lifecycle Workflows budget, administrative unit limits, dynamic units' cloud availability; reviewed with every design change
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Identity engineering Source: ../books/guides/attribute-driven-migration.md#limits

Task.Name: A9.3 A full drift cycle on the whole estate: findings closed at the source; the nightly plan zero-action
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Security operations, with HR Source: ../books/b01-transformation-arc/04-identity-transformation.md#verification

Task.Name: AG9 Gate 9 — Attributes kept true
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: CISO Criteria: Valid attributes for every HR-listed worker; every group on one of the two patterns; every unit rule mirroring its group with processing on; every policy targeting only governed groups; zero open high-severity drift findings; logs outside Entra ID; the six lifecycle metrics on the ConMon cadence Source: ../books/b03-hr-identity/12-execution-plan.md#phase-6-sustained-posture

Task.Name: X-G5 Program G5 — AD Retired
Task.Notes: Owner or approver: Executive sponsor and CIO (program) If decided late: AD is retired with attribute drift still open Source: program-master-schedule.md
